Nope, pineapple doesn't belong, yes, I have that developer background, and yes, I love ownership.
Then you should join Thomas Piccirello and Felipe Almeida on the Security team!

You know what to do ;)

posts.content:
When people come up to me and ask "Jean, what's the best thing you did at the Cirqle" (well ok, not many people come and ask this question; it's a rhetorical device, but let's stay focused please) - I tell them : 

"Well it's simple, we started using PostHog" 

We moved all our dashboards there. We rebuilt our data layer just to build cleaner dashes. We connected our DB to it and connected their MCP to all our tools. Our entire team uses it. 

We discover new use cases all the time. Two weeks ago we started with Replay vision, where Posthog straight up tells you what to fix at scale, looking into a variety of screen recordings. 

This week, Steven Lammertink linked Posthog, Claude and our own home made bug solving platform - we get screen recordings of incidents pulled on slack with an investigation of the issues in real time. Our devs have casual conversations on slack with Posthog about how best to fix our platform.

Just today we caught 2 UI issues no one had reported yet. 

Next month we'll connect the reports to our code directly and start improving things on the fly. 

It's really been transformational; Posthog gives you that feeling of absolute power you had back when you discovered screen recordings existed, 10 or 12 years ago.

Oh and their CEO 🦔 james hawkins writes the best Linkedin posts so that's a bonus.

posts.content:
in the, just over 2.5 years I have been at PostHog, revenue has grown 15x. the Ops team (people & ops(3), talent(6), legal(1), finance(2), compliance(same 1 as legal)) has only grown 6x, and NEWSFLASH, we don't need to grow it that much going forward.

we've grown a lot in my time here but we've managed to keep a pretty lean team to fuel that growth. 

here's what those people actually did:
→ onboarded 200+ new joiners across ~29 countries
→ moved recruiting from 100% inbound to inbound + outbound
→ brought accounting in-house 
→ ripped out the old ERP for an AI-native one (Campfire)
→ built our own ops platform - this is so sick btw
→ held external legal fees FLAT in absolute terms through 15x revenue
→ took employee satisfaction from 83% to 98% (it was 100% one quarter) 🐐 

that's really only scratching the surface

but the honest version isn't "we did more with less". we did a genuinely different job with more people. We could have got by with slightly less, for sure. 

the 6x didn't go on more hands to process the same tickets. it went on people who could delete the tickets - build the platform, own the ledger, run outbound sourcing.
hiring ops people to automate ops work looks like the wrong trade on a headcount plan. however, it's the only one that stops us ballooning headcount from here. 


ps - the 83% → 98% is just from me making excellent contributions in the #dad-jokes slack channel

posts.content:
I already liked PostHog for analytics.
Then I started using the PostHog MCP tooling and it feels slightly magical.
I can work from my coding environment, inspect what’s happening in the product, create or manage feature flags, and reason about user behavior without constantly bouncing between dashboards and tabs.
Then I realized PostHog has feature flags built in too.
So now the loop becomes:
Build → flag it → ship to a subset of users → watch what happens → iterate.
All from a much tighter workflow.
This is what I want AI tooling to feel like. Not another chatbot sitting beside the work, but something that can actually reach into the tools I already use and help me operate them.
MCP is starting to make software development feel less like juggling dashboards and more like having the stack talk back to you.
PostHog + MCP is very, very cool.
Shoutout to all the devs at PostHog, amazing team.
#PostHog #MCP

There's a BRAND NEW trend called "promptless engineering"

And it's (probably) not what you think 👇🏼


I recently came across a new feature by PostHog.

PostHog is a product analytics platform that lets you see or replay user behaviour in your product to make better product decisions.

They just launched a new agent that allows you to turn on "self-driving mode" which is exactly what it sounds like.


Self-driving mode deploys agents into your product analytics, diagnoses problems, fixes bugs, and generates pull requests, all on its own.

To my knowledge, the first of its kind to allow 100% promptless, self-driving agentic coding. 


But what makes this especially interesting, is that even if Anthropic and OpenAI wanted to, they couldn't easily copy it, like they can with every other wrapper.

Because they don't have the depth of product integration and more importantly, the product + user insights PostHog does. 

And maybe that's why they're is growing like CRAZY. 


I decided to hit them up and well, now we're doing an event together. 

If you'd like to learn more about the PostHog approach to agentic engineering, you'll probably benefit from joining our talk in October at Antler.

You'll walk away with new skills, and potentially your very own autonomous self-driving engineer. 👀

repost.content:
We removed spending budgets in Q4 and it barely had any effect on our cash burn. 

Before PostHog raised our Series E I ran a model to project what our cash position would be until the end of 2028. This was in May 2025 and when we closed our July '26 books we were $200k lower than the number we predicted, about ~1% lower. (We're basically running this thing like Enron, I know). 

Now usually this is not something to shout about, but in Q4 '25 we made a big change where we basically removed spending budgets and gave everybody in the company a $5k a month budget on a company card and told them to "spend money in the best interests of PostHog" 

The obvious concern here was people would go crazy, but they haven't. They've treated this responsibly and people are now able to focus more on building rather than admin around spending. 

Trust is an incredibly strong motivator in a strong team.

That's enough seriousness for now, more memes tomorrow.
